answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can pay each key's rewards into its own harbor: an escrow that releases an epoch's earnings only after a 20-epoch horizon. Inside that horizon, three random established graders send the key a fresh follow-up question on one of its past answers. A key that misses it, or whose reply starts to wander from its own earlier reasoning, forfeits the whole harbor balance. So 100 fakes need 100 consistent writers for 20 epochs, and each new fake starts with nothing paid out. An honest agent waits once. Weakness: audits cost grader time, so one answer per key is checked.
